Disjoint by full path.

## 裁决 — triage's grade

Triage seat, 2026-08-24, promoted → `pm:queue`, **Bug**. Verbatim: *"same undeclared-alias read #5344 retired, one file over, and the two surfaces now disagree inside one panel. **Same retirement shape; re-verify the #5344 landing on current main first.**"*

**Read #5344's PR before writing anything** — the fence says to reuse its retirement shape, and this is the sixth site in that family (#5068 renderer, #5120 `packages/components`/`plugin-dashboard`, #5340 `bridgeListView`, #5344 the column inspector) and the second editor-side one.

## Two defects that are NOT in dispute — fix these regardless of how the third resolves

The card names three things, and only one of them is a judgement call. ⛔ Do not let the open question stall the two that are not.

**1. `colLabel`'s precedence is INVERTED, not merely tolerant.** The chain at `:29` is `label ?? header ?? field ?? accessorKey` — `header` is preferred **over** `field`. So a perfectly canonical column that also carries a stray `header` key displays `header`'s value **instead of** its declared `label`/`field`. ⚠️ That is a bug under *every* reading of the third question: even if the list keeps a best-effort fallback, a declared identity must outrank an undeclared alias.

**2. `colFieldName` backs more than a label.** At `:39` it is `o.field ?? o.accessorKey`, and it feeds `usedFieldNames()` — which the Add-field picker uses to decide which object fields are already taken. So **a spec-refused column still reserves a field name in the picker**, hiding a field the author is entitled to add. ⚠️ Also a bug under every reading: whatever the *display* fallback should be, a refused spelling must not consume a name.

## PM建议路线 on the third question — ⛔ a lean, NOT a ruling

The open question is whether `colLabel` should drop its alias fallback entirely (matching #5344) or keep a best-effort human label. The card declines to take it, and names the asymmetry: *"an empty field-key box invites re-authoring, an empty **list row** would leave the author with nothing to click."*

**Lean: follow triage's "same retirement shape" — drop the undeclared aliases — but ⛔ do NOT let a row render nameless.** A column the helper cannot otherwise name should fall through to the existing positional fallback `` `col ${i + 1}` ``, which already exists at the end of that chain and is exactly the "something to click" the asymmetry worries about. That resolves the tension without inventing a new affordance.

⛔ **If your measurement shows that fallback does not actually produce a clickable row** — the list keys on the label, the empty case collapses the row, anything of that shape — ⛔ **stop and report**. That is a UX call for the maintainer, not a dev call and not mine.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **Re-verify the #5344 landing on current `main` first**, as triage instructs. ⚠️ `packages/app-shell` moved twice today (#5565's console-side seam, #5835's `RecordDetailView`), and this seat merged eight PRs. Re-derive `view-column-io.ts:29` and `:39` and the sole-importer claim (`grep -rn "view-column-io" packages/app-shell/src --include=*.tsx`) on your merge-base, and report any delta.
2. ⚠️ **There is an existing pin that ASSERTS THE BUG and is documented to flip.** `ViewColumnInspector.identityRead.test.tsx`, the test named *"records the residue this card is fenced out of"*, asserts `getAllByText('Name')` has length **1** and carries a comment saying the expectation flips when this is fixed. ⛔ Do not read its failure as a regression, and ⛔ do not delete it — **flip it**, and say in the report that you did. A pin written to be flipped is the previous card handing you its receipt.
3. **`usedFieldNames()` is the reachability claim for defect 2.** Verify that `colFieldName` really feeds it and that it really drives the Add-field picker, in those functions' own source. If the chain is broken somewhere, defect 2 is smaller than the card prices and you should say so.

## Verification

**Pin the panel-level disagreement, because that is the actual defect:** one stored column `{accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'}`, one mount, asserting the inspector's identity controls and the list row beside them **agree**. That is the observable the #5344 ruling required and did not get.

Direction predicted **before** running: revert each fix and show its own assertion goes red — the inverted-precedence case and the picker-reservation case are **separate** and need separate legs. **Counter-probe required:** a canonical column (declared `field` + `label`, no aliases) must still show its label in the list **and** still reserve its name in the picker — otherwise "the aliases are gone" is satisfiable by breaking the list and the picker outright.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text; ⚠️ **print the landing site rather than assuming it**, and ⚠️ **assert anchor uniqueness before writing** — both traps were measured in this round (#4730's mis-anchored injection that still moved the number in the predicted direction; #5927's anchor hitting three sites on byte-identical lines). Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

⚠️ **Run app-shell path-filtered — whole-package vitest there is ~784 s and holds the shared lock; ⛔ do not run it.** Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and note a first RED reading `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` is the **unbuilt-closure** signature while `Cannot find module` on a bare package name in a fresh worktree is the **missing-`node_modules`** signature; they need different fixes and #5835 hit the second one today), the path-filtered vitest, eslint on changed files with merge-base delta. ⚠️ Plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`; it manufactures phantom errors (measured twice today).

Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing; empty frontmatter is this repo's "releases nothing" declaration. Draft PR, `Fixes #5725`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM correction — this claim had no worker behind it for ~2h

Same seat, same session (`session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`), so ⛔ this is **not** a second claim and the claim above stands. Recording the gap because it is my error and it cost the card two hours.

The claim comment went up at **14:04:51Z**. The dev agent behind it was **never actually launched** — I posted the atomic claim pair and the dispatch, and then lost the launch across a context boundary. The symptom that surfaced it: `objectui-issue-5725/` does **not exist on disk** while the three other in-flight cards' worktrees do. No worktree, no branch, no PR, no report — the card was locked by a claim and nothing was working it, which is precisely the harm the claim protocol exists to prevent.

**Relaunched at 16:15Z** against the dispatch above, unchanged in substance. Two things were added to it because the gap itself changed the ground:

1. ⚠️ **`main` moved substantially in those two hours** — this seat merged #6066, #6068 and #6072 among others. Assumption 1 (*"re-verify the #5344 landing on current main first"*) was already the card's first instruction; it is now doubly load-bearing, and the dev is told to re-derive **every** line number and **every** claim the card makes rather than carry any of them.
2. ⚠️ **#6072 landed in this card's own directory** — `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/` (`PageBlockCanvas.tsx`, `block-types.ts`) at 15:53Z. Different files from `view-column-io.ts`, so no overlap, but the branch must be cut from a base that contains it.
3. ⚠️ **#6073 landed and widened `check-changeset-presence.mjs`** beyond `/src/` to include the bundler's `index.html` entry and anything a package's own `files` list publishes. The dispatch's changeset instruction now says to run the gate rather than reason from the old rule.

**Process note for this seat, not for this card:** a claim is only honest if a worker exists behind it. Posting the claim pair and launching the worker are now one step, and any card sitting in `pm:dispatched` with no worktree on disk and no report is treated as a stalled claim to be relaunched, not as work in progress.

## Answers to the three PM mechanism assumptions

**1. Re-verified the #5344 landing on current `main`. No delta from the card, but one location correction.**
Merge-base `7c96c9420` (branched from current `origin/main`, which contains #6072 and #6073). #5344 landed as commit `0e00da354` — *"fix(app-shell): read view-column identity in the canonical spelling only (#5726)"* — and its shape is exactly what triage told me to reuse: `colFieldKey` went `c.field ?? c.accessorKey` → `c.field`, `colDisplayLabel` went `c.label ?? c.header ?? colFieldKey(c)` → `c.label ?? colFieldKey(c)`, plus a `minor` changeset and a real-mount pin. My `colLabel` is now the same shape one level out: `label ?? field ?? positional`.

Both cited line numbers hold verbatim on my merge-base: `view-column-io.ts:29` is the `colLabel` chain, `:39` is `colFieldName`'s. The sole-importer claim holds — `grep -rn "view-column-io" packages/app-shell/src --include=*.tsx` returns `FieldsListEditor.tsx:34` (the import) and one comment reference in the inspector's test file; no other importer anywhere in `packages/`.

**Correction to the card and the dispatch, worth recording:** `ViewColumnInspector.tsx` and `ViewColumnInspector.identityRead.test.tsx` do **not** live in `previews/` — they live in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/**inspectors**/`. Only `view-column-io.ts`, `FieldsListEditor.tsx` and `ViewColumnPanes.tsx` are in `previews/`. Nothing turns on it, but the dispatch's file surface named one directory for both halves.

**2. The documented pin was flipped, not deleted — and widened.**
`ViewColumnInspector.identityRead.test.tsx`'s last case asserted `getAllByText('Name')` had length **1** with a comment saying the expectation flips when this card lands. It now asserts `queryAllByText('Name')` has length **0** over the whole panel, that the row is named `col 1`, and that the identity controls are still empty — so "the panel agrees" is a two-sided claim rather than a claim about the list alone. The test was renamed from *"records the residue this card is fenced out of"* to *"the whole panel agrees: no surface presents the refused spelling as an identity"*, and the suite docblock was updated to record that the flip happened rather than leaving a stale "still outstanding" note. The count goes 2 → 1 → 0 across the two cards. This is the observable the #5344 ruling required and did not get.

**3. `usedFieldNames()` is reachable — but defect 2 is smaller than the card priced it.**
The chain is real and I read every link in its own source: `FieldsListEditor.tsx:158` computes `const usedNames = usedFieldNames(columns)` and passes it at `:207` to `AddFieldPopover`, which at `ViewColumnPanes.tsx:323` does `const used = usedNames.has(f.name)`.

But `usedNames` does **not** hide or disable the option. `filtered` is computed from the search query alone; `used` only renders an "Added" `Badge`, and the option's `onClick={() => onAdd(f)}` stays live. So the card's *"hiding a field the author is entitled to add"* overstates it: a spec-refused column **mislabelled** a field as already taken — misleading, and a display alias leaking into a non-display decision — but it never blocked the author from adding it. Real, reachable, observable, and now pinned; just smaller than priced. Recorded in the new test's docblock so the pin says what the mechanism does rather than what was assumed.

## The third question needed no escalation

The PM's lean held under measurement. `FieldListRow` is a `role="button"` div carrying a grip, a field icon, the label span and a remove control — it does not key on the label and does not collapse when the label is empty. And it never is empty: the positional fallback `` `col ${i + 1}` `` already sat at the end of that chain. Measured end-to-end rather than reasoned about: the new component test mounts the real editor with `{accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name'}`, asserts the row reads `col 1`, then **clicks it** and asserts `onSelectionChange` fires with `{kind: 'column', id: 'list.columns[0]', label: 'col 1'}`. The author has something to click. No UX call was needed from the maintainer.

## Deviations from the dispatch

1. **Reported above:** one of my own assertions was non-discriminating and was strengthened mid-verification, after leg A came back 4 red where I had predicted 5.
2. **`gh` is not installed in this container** and direct `curl` to `api.github.com` returns `HTTP 403` from the proxy, so the draft PR was created through the GitHub MCP tool instead. Verified afterwards: `draft: true`, body intact, session-URL footer survived.
3. Reporting at draft-PR time with CI not yet converged, per the standing rule — the PM reads the real gate job conclusions.

⛔ Not marked ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge. Worktree removed cleanly without `--force`.
